nodes.label: Agent Skills portable six-field frontmatter
nodes.summary: Claude Code accepts every frontmatter field, but claude.ai skill uploads, the Skills API and package_skill.py accept only the Agent Skills spec set: name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools. Any other key raises the unexpected-key error on those paths, and Claude Code loads the six-field form unchanged.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - audit-kompatibilitas-skills-md-multi-agent [ses_f12437de6ffejl2if9I0g8pTjZ].md:L1703] Restricting frontmatter to the spec's six fields avoids the unexpected-key error

nodes.label: allowed-tools delimiter portability gap
nodes.summary: The agentskills.io spec writes allowed-tools space-delimited (Read Grep Glob); Claude Code writes it comma-delimited (Read, Grep, Glob). Both spellings are accepted by their own runtime, so the delimiter is the field that silently makes a skill single-vendor.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - audit-kompatibilitas-skills-md-multi-agent [ses_f12437de6ffejl2if9I0g8pTjZ].md:L01984] A skill using space-delimited `allowed-tools` is cross-vendor portable.

nodes.label: Canonical .agents/skills/ dir with byte-identical mirrors
nodes.summary: T1-spec decision 1: one canonical tree at .agents/skills/<slug>/ plus byte-identical COPIES into .claude/, .gemini/, .opencode/ and .cursor/ skills dirs, so each vendor loader finds its own path without resolving anything at read time.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - audit-kompatibilitas-skills-md-multi-agent [ses_f12437de6ffejl2if9I0g8pTjZ].md:L05659] Canonical `.agents/skills/<slug>/` + byte-identical COPIES (not symlinks) to `.claude/.gemini/.opencode/.cursor/skills/` — symlinks break on Windows checkouts and Pages builds.

nodes.label: Thin SKILL.md plus verbatim full-instructions reference
nodes.norm_label: thin skill.md plus verbatim full-instructions reference
nodes.summary: T1-spec decision 3: SKILL.md carries at most a 15-step workflow plus a pointer, while the source instruction text is copied verbatim into references/full-instructions.md; frontmatter stays limited to name/description/license/metadata. Later measured across all 190 skills: 188 of the reference files are byte-identical 1:1 to the track-page source text, 2 differ for reasons outside the generator (L21900).

nodes.label: Skill body byte budget against the validator token ceiling
nodes.norm_label: skill body byte budget against the validator token ceiling
nodes.summary: validate-skills.ts failed one skill with body ~5599 tokens (tokens = ceil(bytes/4), max 5000) because the generator's body-vs-references split let a ~22k-char Gemini section stay inline. The fix adds a render() closure with an enforcement loop: while byteLength(body) > 19000 (headroom under the 20000-byte ceiling) drop trailing steps, then trailing kapan bullets, then hard-shrink to 100 chars, never touching template sections or the references pointer.

nodes.label: Static asset serving replaces the node:fs skill route
nodes.norm_label: static asset serving replaces the node:fs skill route
nodes.summary: The first delivery shape was an /api/skills/<slug> route reading through node:fs with an allowlist. It worked locally and 404ed on Cloudflare. The replacement publishes each SKILL.md as a static asset at <base>/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md; the route and its resolver were deleted and verified live as HTTP 200 with correct frontmatter.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - audit-kompatibilitas-skills-md-multi-agent [ses_f12437de6ffejl2if9I0g8pTjZ].md:L8135] node:fs throws on workerd with no nodejs_compat flag, so the route degrades to 404 on Cloudflare

nodes.label: Manifest written only when content changes
nodes.norm_label: manifest written only when content changes
nodes.summary: skills-manifest.json was not byte-identical across regeneration because generated_at was rewritten on every run (4622c7 -> 5e6dc0) even while all 190 SKILL.md hashes stayed identical. The manifest is now written only when content changes, so double regeneration is byte-identical and the timestamp means the time of the content change; spec section 6 was amended.

nodes.label: Stale Astro digest fast-path store in node_modules
nodes.norm_label: stale astro digest fast-path store in node_modules
nodes.summary: Converting MDX pages to plain .md broke the build, but not because of the conversion. The content was byte-identical, so Astro's digest fast-path never updated the stored filePath, and the live store is node_modules/.astro/data-store.json rather than the project's .astro/ directory. Traced via strace, the loader, and instrumentation; recorded in the plan Error Ledger. Fix is clearing the cache once; fresh installs and CI are unaffected.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - audit-kompatibilitas-skills-md-multi-agent [ses_f12437de6ffejl2if9I0g8pTjZ].md:L14108] The build break came from the stale digest store, not from the conversion

nodes.label: Bare base URL 404 from Worker route pattern mismatch
nodes.norm_label: bare base url 404 from worker route pattern mismatch
nodes.summary: Root cause 1 of 2: the route .../fasttrack/dashboard/* never matches a URL without a trailing slash, so the request fell through to the Azure nginx origin and returned the origin's 404. That is the 'Halaman tidak ditemukan' anyone typing the raw URL sees. Fixed by an explicit bare route; live bare -> 307 to the slashed form -> 200.

nodes.label: OAuth success callback redirects to the bare URL
nodes.norm_label: oauth callback redirects to the bare url
nodes.summary: Root cause 2 of 2: the OAuth callback sent a successful login to the slashless URL, so every newly logged-in user landed exactly on the bug, and it was the only publisher of that Location in the whole repo. Fixed by adding the slash to the callback Location, two lines total.

nodes.label: Starlight 404 page leaks into the autogenerated sidebar
nodes.norm_label: starlight 404 page leaks into the autogenerated sidebar
nodes.summary: Read from Starlight 0.42.0 source, not guessed: the 404 page must stay in the docs collection because routing/data.js:117 fetches it with getEntry("docs", "404"), but the autogenerated sidebar filters only on !sidebar.hidden (navigation.js:133) with a default of false (schema.js:70). So the 404.md added to silence a build warning became a nav item on every page. Fix is frontmatter sidebar.hidden: true alone; the file is not moved and the real 404 keeps working.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - audit-kompatibilitas-skills-md-multi-agent [ses_f12437de6ffejl2if9I0g8pTjZ].md:L17664] Verify the URLs the user clicked, not the ones chosen in-house

nodes.label: download attribute decides save over inline render
nodes.norm_label: download attribute decides save over inline render
nodes.summary: The download links were plain [Unduh SKILL.md](...) anchors with no download attribute, and the file was served as text/markdown with no Content-Disposition, so the browser read it as a document and opened it in a tab. Fix is an inline-HTML anchor with download="<slug>.skill.md" plus the generator's own link updated so regeneration cannot reintroduce the bug; the response stays 200 text/markdown.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-fasttrack/2026-09-29 - audit-kompatibilitas-skills-md-multi-agent [ses_f12437de6ffejl2if9I0g8pTjZ].md:L22893] The download attribute, not the content type, is what makes the browser save
